s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Diagnosed with COVID-19 three weeks prior to presentation
Developed rhinorrhea and recovered from COVID-19
Worsening right-sided headache started 1 week after COVID-19 recovery
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells

shortlist.label: Orbital Apex Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone and extension of inflammation into the apex

shortlist.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Rhinorrhea and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement

shortlist.label: IgG4-related Orbital Inflammatory Pseudotumor
shortlist.why_kept: Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells and orbital inflammation

raw.rationale: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive, are key evidence-based reasons

rejected.label: Orbital Apex Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms consistent with Orbital Apex Syndrome, such as vision loss and severe pain on ocular motion, the elevated IgG4 level and histopathologic findings are more specific for IgG4-related disease

rejected.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of fungal elements in the pathology report and the patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings are not typical for invasive aspergillosis

rejected.label: Mucormycosis
rejected.why: Similar to invasive aspergillosis, there is no evidence of fungal infection and the patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings are not consistent with mucormycosis

rejected.label: IgG4-related Orbital Inflammatory Pseudotumor
rejected.why: While this diagnosis could explain some of the patient's symptoms, the involvement of multiple sinuses and the specific histopathologic findings make IgG4-related disease a more comprehensive diagnosis
